title: bug: the lander answers NOTHING_TO_COMMIT before it checks the workspace against the verified tree
definitionOfDone: A test stages the reproduction through the production writers - verify a real change, restore the original bytes, then land - and asserts the lander does NOT answer a bare no-effect success. Assert the specific stable refusal code and its layer, not merely that it did not commit.

The workspace-versus-verified-tree check runs on the zero-delivered-paths path. Prove it by a verified-workspace port that throws if never consulted, so the arm cannot pass while the check is skipped.

A genuine no-op still succeeds: a node that ran, was accepted, and truly had nothing to commit still reaches its existing no-effect outcome and is still credited by `landedWithNoEffect`. Name the existing arm in goal-landing-facts or its siblings that proves the credit path is unbroken.
Non-vacuity: move the early return back above the verification check and confirm the new arm goes red. Quote the red.
`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` EXIT 0 with the `Test Files N passed (N)` count line quoted.

implementationPlan.description:
WRITE THE FAILING ARM FIRST. This is DoD item 1 and it must go red before any production edit.

Stage the review's reproduction through the production writers: a node whose verifier receipt binds a workspace that WAS changed and accepted, then restore the original bytes so the workspace no longer matches the accepted binding, then land. Today the lander answers NOTHING_TO_COMMIT because the zero-delivered branch returns first.

Assert the SPECIFIC stable refusal code AND its layer - LANDING_VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_CHANGED - not merely that it did not commit and not merely that it refused. A bare 'refused' assertion is one added layer away from vacuous here, because several refusals are reachable on this path.

Also assert no commit was made and the durable landing receipt records that same code, mirroring how the neighbouring arms read the receipt back from the store rather than trusting the report.

Run it and QUOTE THE RED. A test that does not fail first has not earned its place.
implementationPlan.note:
FAILING ARM WRITTEN FIRST, RED QUOTED. No production byte changed in this step.

Added to node-lander.test.ts:
 - `countedWorkspace(git, captured)` helper: a VerifiedWorkspacePort that counts captures and exposes `assertConsulted()`, which THROWS `VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_NEVER_CONSULTED` when the count is zero. This is the DoD-item-2 probe and it is reusable by the genuine-no-op arm in step 5.
 - arm "refuses a workspace restored to its staffed state after a different state was verified".

HOW IT STAGES THE REPRODUCTION THROUGH THE PRODUCTION WRITERS. `made.baseline(NODE)` records the staffing baseline through `recordLandingBaseline` (the real writer), observing one operator-dirty path. `readVerifiedBinding` returns a binding with treeSha "3"*40 — the workspace as the verifier accepted it, with the seat's edit present. The port then captures BINDING (treeSha "2"*40) — the workspace RESTORED to its staffed bytes. The land-time observation equals the baseline observation exactly, so `deliveredPaths` is empty and the zero-delivered branch is the ONLY branch that can answer. The receipt is read back out of the store via `readLandingReceipt`, not trusted from the report.

WHAT IT ASSERTS — code AND layer, not "it refused". It asserts the WHOLE report deep-equals the exact code/detail pair "LANDING_VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_CHANGED: current workspace differs from the verified candidate". That sentence is authored at exactly one place in the tree, node-lander-verification.ts:32-34, so it pins WHICH LAYER answered; the lander's own refusals and the commit port's refusals all carry different prose. Deep-equalling the whole report also states positively that the answer is NOT NOTHING_TO_COMMIT, which a `.not.toContain` would only state weakly. Then: `git.commits` is empty, `assertConsulted()` (an independent guard so the arm cannot pass if a later edit answers the right code WITHOUT consulting the tree), and the durable receipt's `refusal.code` plus a null commit.

THE RED, verbatim, from `npx vitest run --root . --config package.json --testTimeout=30000 -t "restored to its staffed state" src/orchestrator/node-lander.test.ts` (PIPESTATUS[0]=1):

  FAIL  src/orchestrator/node-lander.test.ts > createNodeLander > refuses a workspace restored to its staffed state after a different state was verified
  AssertionError: expected [ { …(3) } ] to deeply equal [ { …(3) } ]
  - Expected
  + Received
    [
      {
  -     "detail": "LANDING_VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_CHANGED: current workspace differs from the verified candidate",
  +     "detail": "NOTHING_TO_COMMIT: no path in the workspace differs from the staffing baseline",
        "nodeRef": "node-land-1",
        "outcome": "REFUSED",
      },
    ]
   Test Files  1 failed (1)
   Tests  1 failed | 19 skipped (20)

That received line IS the defect: the lander answered "no path differs from the staffing baseline" about a workspace that no longer matches the tree the verifier accepted.

A SECOND, INDEPENDENT RED WAS ALSO OBSERVED. On the first run I had `assertConsulted()` placed before the code assertion; it fired first with `Error: VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_NEVER_CONSULTED` at node-lander.test.ts:83. I then moved it AFTER the code assertion so the primary red quotes the wrong ANSWER rather than the missing call — but both reds are real and independent, and together they say the check is not merely returning the wrong code, it is never reached at all on this path.

Arm count moved 19 -> 20 in this file, as expected for one added arm.

implementationPlan.description:
THE MINIMUM IMPLEMENTATION: hoist the check, change nothing else.

Move the checkLandingVerification block ABOVE the zero-delivered early return in node-lander.ts. Hold its result in scope so commitJournaledLanding still receives checked.binding and checked.port; do not call it twice.

Do NOT mint a new refusal code, do not add a layer constant, do not touch the NOTHING_TO_COMMIT literal or its detail string - twenty files reference that code and this row does not change its meaning.

Two properties to preserve and to state in the step note:
  - The refusal is still decided BEFORE any journal write. checkLandingVerification performs no journal write, so hoisting keeps the effect-free-before-journal property that the 'records the NOTHING_TO_COMMIT refusal with no journaled landing intent' arm exists to guard. That arm must stay green WITHOUT being edited.
  - A world that is both unconfigured and zero-delivered now answers the verification refusal rather than NOTHING_TO_COMMIT. That is intended; say so explicitly so a reviewer does not read it as an accident.

Run the step 2 arm and confirm it is now green.
implementationPlan.note:
MINIMUM IMPLEMENTATION LANDED: a pure move of the `checkLandingVerification` block from below the zero-delivered early return to above it, plus a 5-line comment saying why the order matters. `git diff --stat` is `10 insertions(+), 5 deletions(-)` — 5 moved lines out, the same 5 back in at the new position, and 5 new comment lines. node-lander.ts 272 -> 277 lines, under the 400 split threshold.

The step-2 arm is now GREEN: `Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 1 passed | 19 skipped (20)`, PIPESTATUS[0]=0.

WHAT I DID NOT DO, as instructed. No new refusal code. No new `*_LAYER` constant (which would force a roster backfill across the closed code-to-layer map). The NOTHING_TO_COMMIT literal and its detail string "no path in the workspace differs from the staffing baseline" are byte-identical to HEAD — confirmed in the diff, the hunk shows them as unchanged context. `checkLandingVerification` is called exactly once; `checked.binding` and `checked.port` are still the values handed to `commitJournaledLanding`, now from a binding declared earlier in the same scope.

PROPERTY 1 — THE REFUSAL IS STILL DECIDED BEFORE ANY JOURNAL WRITE, PRESERVED. `checkLandingVerification` (node-lander-verification.ts, 36 lines, read in full) performs no store write at all: it reads a verifier receipt, calls `port.capture`, and compares. The only journal write on this path is inside `commitJournaledLanding`, which is still strictly below both refusals. So the effect-free-before-journal property that the "records the NOTHING_TO_COMMIT refusal with no journaled landing intent" arm exists to guard is intact, and that arm is UNEDITED — I did not touch it.

PROPERTY 2 — INTENDED ORDERING CHANGE, STATED SO NO REVIEWER READS IT AS AN ACCIDENT. A world that is BOTH unconfigured (or holds a legacy receipt with no workspace binding) AND zero-delivered now answers the verification refusal — LANDING_VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_UNCONFIGURED or LANDING_VERIFIER_BINDING_MISSING — rather than NOTHING_TO_COMMIT. That is deliberate and is the point of the row: "no path differs from the staffing baseline" is an evidentiary claim, and a lander that cannot see the verified candidate has no standing to make it. Production is unaffected in the configured case: repository-delivery-runtime.ts:71,:79-80 passes `verifiedWorkspace` unconditionally, so a genuine no-op in production still captures successfully, compares equal, and falls through to NOTHING_TO_COMMIT exactly as before.

COST: one extra `port.capture()` on the genuine-no-op path, where previously there was none. Production already captures on every other landing path, and the capture is a Git read with no effect.

Step 4 now settles the flipped arms against the step-1 prediction.

implementationPlan.note:
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW DONE. One real out-of-scope defect found and filed; no in-scope fix needed. Full completion evidence is in comment-b0666f0f1515423da6908201ff3bf11f.

Q1 — CAN THE HOISTED CHECK COMPARE AGAINST A STALE BINDING? No. In production readVerifiedBinding is absent, so the binding is read from the receipt whose id is the EXACT accepted verifierReceiptId, and node-lander-verification.ts:24-26 additionally requires subjectRef, workspace and test to match the brief. A re-verification mints a new receipt id, and therefore a new acceptance and a new landing receipt id. The hoist changes WHEN that read happens, not WHICH binding is read. It opens no new staleness vector: the delivered path already performed this identical read before the row.

Q2 — A NODE WITH NO VERIFIER RECEIPT? It cannot reach the check: readAccepted returns null and landOnce skips it. An ACCEPTED node whose receipt carries no matching binding now answers LANDING_VERIFIER_BINDING_MISSING on a zero-delivered workspace, where it used to answer NOTHING_TO_COMMIT and be credited. That is the right answer — "we cannot see the tree we accepted" must not be credited as "provably owed nothing" — and it is the answer a reader would expect. It is NOT retroactive: landOne returns null for any acceptance that already has a landing receipt, so every NOTHING_TO_COMMIT receipt written before this row keeps its credit.

Q3 — DOUBLE CAPTURE, OR CAPTURE BEFORE A CHEAPER REFUSAL? No double capture. There is exactly one checkLandingVerification call site; the old one is deleted in the diff. `grep capture node-lander-journal.ts` returns nothing, so commitJournaledLanding does not capture again. Every refusal that answered before the check still answers before it: receipt exists, journal gate, missing brief, missing baseline, observe failure. Only NOTHING_TO_COMMIT moved below it, which is the point. The cost is one extra git read per genuine no-op. Capture runs with GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 on a scratch GIT_INDEX_FILE, so it takes no lock on the real index.

Q4 — REFUSAL STILL DECIDED BEFORE EVERY JOURNAL WRITE, ON EVERY PATH? Yes. checkLandingVerification only reads. refuse() writes a landing RECEIPT, never an intent. The only intent write is inside commitJournaledLanding, strictly below both refusals. Empirical proof: "records the NOTHING_TO_COMMIT refusal with no journaled landing intent" stayed green UNEDITED, and its readRepositoryLandingEvidence assertion is REPOSITORY_RECOVERY_EVIDENCE_MISSING.

Q5 — COULD A GENUINE NO-OP SILENTLY STOP COUNTING? Not in production's configured path. The port is passed unconditionally, every receipt the current verifier mints carries a workspaceBinding, and repository-delivery-runtime.test.ts proves it end to end over real git and a real store: landedWithNoEffect === true through a REAL verifier receipt. The genuine-no-op consultation arm makes restoring the early return fail loudly even though the ANSWER would still be right. The only no-ops that stop counting are the fail-closed cases in Q2, plus a no-op whose HEAD moved between verification and landing. That one now answers LANDING_VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_CHANGED, consistent with how the delivered path has always treated a moved HEAD. Per-root reservation serialization makes it rare.

RACES. There is now an await between observe computing delivered=[] and the NOTHING_TO_COMMIT decision. A workspace edit in that gap is seen by capture, the bindings differ, and the landing is REFUSED. Every race outcome is a refusal, never a false credit. The same observe-then-capture gap already existed on the delivered path.

REAL DEFECT FOUND, OUT OF SCOPE, FILED as task-cab96ebcd3b6403cbbf412bdad839403 (PLANNING, MEDIUM, dependsOn this row because both edit landOne). Every checkLandingVerification failure is recorded durably and never retried. Capture can fail transiently: VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_DRIFT when HEAD moves mid-capture (git-verified-workspace-capture.ts:63), and VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_GIT_FAILED on a 30s git timeout. The lander's own observe path follows the opposite rule ("reported, not recorded: the next pass retries").
